TEXT.TEXTVALUE: Take a small quantity of ferrous sulphate crystals (FeSO4.7H2O) in a dry boiling tube.
Hold the boiling tube with a test tube holder.
Heat the boiling tube over the flame of a burner.
On heating ferrous sulphate crystals, they lose their water molecules and form white coloured crystals of anhydrous ferrous sulphate (FeSO4).

On further heating, anhydrous ferrous sulphate decomposes to form dark brown coloured ferric oxide (Fe2O3), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and sulphur trioxide (SO3) gases. The gas emitted has the odour of burning sulphur.
In this reaction a single reactant FeSO4 decomposes to form three different products Fe2O3(s), SO2(g) and SO3(g). So the reaction is a decomposition reaction.
